description:
Maintainer request, 2026-08-13 07:2x (filed outside active hours; no audit or code work done -- no unwrap count taken yet).

Motivation: the op-m1jz crash. A recoverable ThermophysicalPropertyTemperatureRangeError was .unwrap()ed in one_d_solid_array_with_lateral_coupling/calculation.rs:95, which killed the whole htgr_sim_v1 process and reported no material, no node, and no temperature. That single unwrap is a symptom; the maintainer wants the pattern removed across TUAS so the library fails gracefully and the caller can decide what to do.

STEP 0 -- AUDIT BEFORE EDITING. Count and classify every .unwrap() / .expect() in crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver/src/. Report the number and the breakdown before changing anything; the result decides whether this stays one bead or becomes an epic with per-module children.

CLASSIFICATION -- these are NOT all the same defect, and a blanket sed would be wrong:
  (a) Recoverable domain errors (property out of range, convergence failure, bad geometry, empty collection) -- THESE ARE THE TARGET. Propagate through TUAS's existing error enum; do not invent a parallel error type without checking what the crate already has.
  (b) Lock poisoning on RwLock/Mutex -- very common in this codebase's Arc<RwLock<T>> state. Decide a single consistent policy rather than case-by-case.
  (c) Genuinely infallible (a just-inserted key, a statically-known-nonempty vec). Leaving these is acceptable, but each should say WHY in a short comment, or be restructured so the invariant is visible.
  (d) Tests / examples -- OUT OF SCOPE. unwrap in a test is fine and should be left alone.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Replacing .unwrap() with .expect("...") is NOT a fix -- it still panics. Only better as a stopgap on category (c).
- Error messages must carry the diagnostic payload the panic lacked: which component/node, what value, what the allowed range was.
- Changing public fn signatures to return Result is a BREAKING API CHANGE for TUAS's dependents (tampines, teh-o-prke dev-deps, nee_soon, the digital-twin engine). Expect a compile cascade; that is the compiler doing its job, per the workspace rename guidance. Do NOT bump the crate version -- versions are only bumped when the maintainer explicitly asks.
- Callers that genuinely cannot recover (a GUI render loop) should surface the error to the user and keep running or shut down cleanly, not re-unwrap it one level up. Moving the panic up a frame is not the deliverable.
- Release-mode build/test rule applies: cargo check --workspace --lib --tests, cargo test --release.

Related: op-m1jz (the crash that motivated this).

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
AUDIT COMPLETE, 2026-08-13 (read-only agent; counts measured by a brace-depth-aware Python walk over src/, not eyeballed).

HEADLINE: 5025 raw occurrences, 4929 live (96 in commented-out code), across 203 files. But 3823 are TEST code and out of scope.
  (a) recoverable domain error ....... 833   <- the target
  (a/c) into()/try_into() HTE conv ... 245   <- genuinely ambiguous, needs type info to split
  (b) lock poisoning + join .......... 26
  (c) genuinely infallible ........... 2
Plus a second panic class the brief missed: 166 panicking MACROS in library paths (panic! x125, todo! x18, unimplemented! x2, unreachable! x0).
Work estimate for bucket (a): ~975 sites, up to 245 more depending on the conversion judgement.

MY BRIEF'S PREMISE ON LOCKS WAS WRONG. This crate contains ZERO RwLock (grep -c RwLock src/ = 0). The primitive is Arc<Mutex<T>>, and there are only 22 .lock().unwrap() sites, in four files -- three of which are inside functions literally named _advance_timestep_parallel_buggy. Bucket (b) is a rounding error, not a policy problem: one PoisonedLock variant plus a .map_err() helper covers all 26 including the 4 join() sites.

THE SINGLE HIGHEST-VALUE FINDING -- the error variant carries no payload.
  TuasLibError lives at src/lib/tuas_lib_error/mod.rs (NOT tuas_lib_error.rs), 9 variants.
  ThermophysicalPropertyTemperatureRangeError is a UNIT variant. That is precisely why the htgr_sim_v1 crash reported no
  material, no node and no temperature. Even a perfect ?-propagation pass would still produce an unactionable message.
  Adding fields to it is arguably worth more than removing any single unwrap, and it is non-API-breaking (constructed in
  ~40 places, all as a bare unit value).

THE MOTIVATING CRASH IS A FREE FIX -- ZERO API CHANGE.
  advance_timestep ALREADY returns Result<(), TuasLibError> in both array modules (one_d_solid_array/calculation.rs:21,
  one_d_fluid_array/calculation.rs:22). So calculation.rs:95 and its twin at one_d_fluid_array/calculation.rs:127 convert
  with no signature change at all.
  Shape caveat: Array1 does not have the Result FromIterator blanket impl, so it needs collect::<Result<Vec<_>,_>>()? then
  Array1::from_vec -- one extra allocation per node-array per timestep. Short-circuits, so not measurably slower, but
  worth benchmarking since it runs per node per timestep.

BLAST RADIUS (grep-based, no LSP available to the agent; downstream figures +/-30%).
  Of 1084 non-lock library sites: 85 pub fns ALREADY return Result (free), 16 private already Result (free),
  174 private plain-return (internal only), 809 pub plain-return (API-BREAKING).
  Of the 166 lib panic-macros, 60 are already inside Result-returning fns (free).
  => COMBINED FREE, NON-BREAKING WORK: ~187 sites, ~19% of the total, zero downstream impact.
  The 809 breaking sites live in 125 distinct pub fns, but only 25 of those are referenced downstream, and 95%+ of the
  ~499 downstream call sites are in examples/ and src/bin/, not downstream library code.
  Per crate: digital-twin-engine 377, tampines 43, tampines-steam-tables 40, teh-o-prke 39, nee_soon 0 (does not depend on TUAS).
  Three names dominate: pipe_fluid_array_temperature (191), advance_timestep (126), calibrate_insulation_thickness (101).
  DUPLICATION MULTIPLIER: examples/fhr_sim_v*/app/thermal_hydraulics_backend/mod.rs exists in FOUR near-identical copies
  (34 call sites each) across tampines, digital-twin-engine, teh-o-prke, tampines-steam-tables. Fixing one means fixing four.

MISSING ERROR VARIANTS for bucket (a): root-finding/convergence failure; lock poisoning; correlation validity-range
  (distinct from property-table range -- 95 panic! in nusselt_number_correlations/pipe_correlations.rs say things like
  'gnielinski Re > 1e6, too high'); nonphysical input (20 panic! in dimensionalisation.rs); general empty-collection
  (CourantMassFlowVectorEmpty is hyper-specific); singular matrix (MatrixError::Singular{col} exists at matrix.rs:39 but
  its one call site flattens it into GenericStringError, losing the column index).

ON op-t647 (the tampines-steam-tables Result facade): the agent recommends TUAS should NOT copy the facade pattern.
  That facade exists because its internals are a large panicking mass nobody wants to re-sign. TUAS is the opposite --
  its property layer ALREADY returns Result correctly (range_check works); the panics are entirely in CALLERS. A facade
  would paper over a problem one level up. What TUAS should share with op-t647 is the ERROR VOCABULARY, not the structure,
  so steam_generator.rs handles one shape of error from both crates. Coordinate variant naming before either side freezes.

Child issues C1-C8 filed separately.

title: TUAS: remove .unwrap() from library paths so failures propagate gracefully instead of panicking
